conceptName: How SDM is built (two repos, one app)

options.text: An Angular SPA front-end and an ASP.NET Core back-end
A SQL database project and a reporting service
Two separate Angular apps, one per environment
A mobile app and a desktop app

items.explanation: SupplementalDataManagerClient is the Angular SPA; SupplementalDataManager is the ASP.NET Core backend that hosts it and serves the API.

misconceptions.b: The database is DDH/SchoolObjectModel, accessed by the backend — not one of SDM's two repos.
misconceptions.c: There's one SPA repo, deployed per environment via config, not a repo per environment.
misconceptions.d: SDM is a web app, not a mobile/desktop pair.

items.stem: Which statement about the ASP.NET Core backend is correct?

options.text: It only exposes the /api/* endpoints; a separate server hosts the SPA
It both hosts the Angular SPA (from wwwroot) and exposes the /api/* REST controllers
It runs the Angular build at request time in the browser
It connects to the database without EF Core, using raw files

items.explanation: The backend does both jobs from one origin: it serves the built SPA out of wwwroot and exposes ~30 REST controllers under /api/*.

misconceptions.a: There's no separate SPA host — the same backend serves both the SPA and the API.
misconceptions.c: The SPA is pre-built and served as static files; the backend doesn't compile Angular per request.
misconceptions.d: Data access is through EF Core against the SchoolObjectModel database.

items.stem: Put a browser request for a data screen in the order it flows through SDM.

options.text: ASP.NET Core backend handles the request
EF Core reads/writes the SchoolObjectModel database

items.explanation: Browser → backend → EF Core → SchoolObjectModel DB. The backend is the single hop between the SPA and the database.

options.text: The name of the SQL database
The sub-path the Angular SPA is mounted under (its base-href and the backend route must match)

items.explanation: The SPA is built with --base-href Iapetus and served at /Iapetus/*; both repos must agree on the name (the backend has a matching IapetusController route).

misconceptions.a: The database is SchoolObjectModel (DDH), not Iapetus.
misconceptions.c: Authentication is Entra ID; Iapetus is just the SPA mount path.
misconceptions.d: Deployments are manual today; Iapetus isn't a pipeline.

items.stem: At deploy time, what has to happen with the Angular build output, and why?
rubric: The Angular app is built and its dist/ output is copied into the backend's wwwroot/
Because the backend hosts the SPA from one origin (so the same app serves both the SPA and /api/*)
items.sampleAnswer: You build the Angular app and copy its dist/supplemental-data-manager output into the backend's wwwroot/. The backend serves those files, so the SPA and the /api/* endpoints come from one app and one origin.
